ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (as amended by Law No. 36 of 2014 and Law No. 4 of 2021); Executive Regulations of the AML Law issued by Decision of the Prime Minister No. 2393 of 2003; Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) AML/CFT Regulations (2020, updated 2021); Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 (as amended); Executive Regulations of the Companies Law (Decree No. 96 of 1982); Law No. 4 of 2018 amending the AML Law to address UBO registers; General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) Implementing Rules and the GAFI UBO Registration Manual.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the corporate shareholder

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory real-time screening of all UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories against: (i) the Egyptian AML/CFT Sanctions List issued by the National Committee for Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing; (ii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List; (iii) United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) EU Consolidated Sanctions List; (v) CBE Blacklist and other local regulatory watchlists. Full name, date of birth, nationality, and passport number matching using fuzzy algorithms and sanctions list permanent identifiers. Enhanced due diligence (EDD) automatically triggered if a match is suspected or if the client is identified as a politically exposed person (PEP). PEP status extends to family members and close associates. The compliance officer must document the rationale for any false-positive clearing, and all clearances must be dated and signed by an independent AML compliance officer within the law firm or the GAFI-approved service provider.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones) — Corporate Registration Portal (as operating via the GAFI 'Tawteen' / Companies Registration Module); also available through the electronic companies registry of the Egyptian Ministry of Justice (Companies' Registry).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Every corporate name must be registered in Arabic using the standard Arabic alphabet. In the certificate of incorporation, the name shall be shown in Arabic as the primary legal name, with a transliterated phonetic English version for international trade purposes. The transliteration must follow a consistent Latin-script mapping as per GAFI administrative directives, and the English name must be audibly and visually equivalent to the Arabic name. No Latin numerals are allowed unless they form part of a standard business abbreviation (e.g., LLC).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Islamic Finance (requiring Sharia supervisory board approval)
Any name of a living or deceased Egyptian public figure without a notarized authorization
Any expression that contradicts public order or morals in the Arab Republic of Egypt
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within five business days of a formal rejection notice, the incorporator or its legal counsel may file a written administrative appeal with the GAFI Corporate Names Committee, attaching: (a) the original reservation request receipt; (b) the rejection notification; (c) a reasoned statement demonstrating that the rejected name does not conflict with any of the statutory grounds; and (d) a notarized board resolution authorizing the appeal. The Names Committee must issue a decision within fifteen business days. If the appeal is denied, the applicant may file a second-level petition before the Egyptian Administrative Court within sixty days from the date of notification. Where the rejection is based on similarity with an existing registered name, the appellant may obtain a non-opposition letter (authorization letter) from the prior trademark or corporate name owner and resubmit the name with that consent. There is no extension of the 30-day name reservation on administrative appeal unless the reserved name is renewed by paying an additional reservation fee before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Accepted only for initial incorporation filing at GAFI, subject to mandatory physical office location being declared within 30 days of incorporation for the LLC to open a bank account and to obtain any operating licenses. For LegalTech SaaS (ISIC 6201), a virtual office can be maintained only as an auxiliary administrative address, but a physical rented or owned office with a lease registered with the Revenue Authority is essential to satisfy Egyptian economic substance inspections and to obtain a tax card. Virtual office addresses are not accepted on the certificate of incorporation, on VAT registration, or on tax invoices.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 60% likelihood within the first 12 months of incorporation, increased to 80% if the LLC applies for value-added tax registration or requests a certificate of compliance with the Companies Law. GAFI and the Egyptian Tax Authority may perform unannounced inspections to verify the registered office's existence, signage, and employee presence. The risk is higher for foreign-owned LLCs operating under the Free Zones regime and for any entity considered to fall within the enhanced monitoring categories.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 on Joint-Stock Companies, Partnerships Limited by Shares and Limited Liability Companies (as amended by Law No. 4 of 2018), read with Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 and its Executive Regulations; limited liability companies are governed by Articles 102–156 of the Companies Law.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration Department, One-Stop Shop, Cairo, Arab Republic of Egypt.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Incorporation Contract (Aqd Al-Ta’sis) combining the Memorandum of Association and Articles of Association, complemented by Commercial Registry Application Form No. 1.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum aggregate paid-up capital applies to LLCs under Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended; however, the entire share capital must be fully subscribed, allocated in equal quota-shares with equal nominal value, and may be contributed in cash or in-kind (in-kind contributions require a founders' valuation report). No blocked escrow or bank deposit certificate is required for LLC formation before the GAFI; capital sufficiency is evaluated against the business plan and the company's corporate object.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD AND SHAREHOLDERS' RESOLUTION of [Company Name] LLC, adopted on the date of issuance of the Commercial Registry certificate: 1. The incorporation contract (Memorandum and Articles of Association) is hereby ratified in its notarized form. 2. The subscription to the entire share capital and the contribution of each founding quota-holder are approved and recorded in the statutory ledger. 3. The registered office is established at the address stated in the incorporation contract in Cairo, Arab Republic of Egypt. 4. [Manager 1] and [Manager 2] are appointed as the first managers, acting jointly. 5. The managers are authorized to complete tax, social insurance, data protection, electronic signature, and banking formalities and to execute all related documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – One-Stop Shop (Invest in Egypt e-Portal and local GAFI desk)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File at least two proposed Arabic and/or English corporate names through the GAFI one-stop-shop portal or in-person desk; obtain an automatic conflict and blacklist clearance against the Commercial Registry database; reserve the approved name for 30 days, renewable once, pending notarization; pay the reservation fee via Fawry or bank transfer; retain the name reservation certificate for the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Proposed reserved corporate names (Arabic and English)
Copy of each founding shareholder's national ID or passport
Draft corporate object aligned with ISIC 6201 (software development, cloud document automation, e-signature authentication)
Power of attorney of the formation agent, if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for similarity or prohibited wording, the applicant may file an administrative objection with the GAFI Name Clearance Committee within 15 days and submit a revised second-choice name without an additional reservation charge.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Incorporation Contract (Memorandum and Articles of Association)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public Office (Ma'mouriyat Al-Shahr Al-Aqari), Ministry of Justice – local district notary in the intended registered-office governorate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founding quota-holders must appear in person or through notarized attorneys to sign the dual-purpose incorporation contract, which sets forth the company's name, object, registered office address, share capital split, quota values, and management structure; the notary authenticates the signatures, verifies the legal capacity of the founders, affixes the stamp duty, and issues the notarization reference; the notary forwards the contract for electronic statutory book capture.
required_dossiers: Fully drafted Arabic incorporation contract in two original copies
Valid original national IDs or passports of all founding quota-holders
Lease contract for the registered office and a no-objection letter from the landlord
Capital records evidencing fully subscribed quotas; valuation report for any in-kind contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary flags a defect (missing spousal consent, capital valuation gap, or incomplete object), the document is returned for amendment and re-signing; founders must cure the defect and re-present within 30 days or file an objection under the Notarization Law before the competent administrative court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registration and GAFI Incorporation Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI – Commercial Registry Department, One-Stop Shop
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarized incorporation contract together with the GAFI application and Commercial Registry Application Form No. 1; the one-stop-shop coordinates simultaneous clearance with the Commercial Registry; upon payment of the statutory filing fees and approval, GAFI issues the Commercial Registry certificate and the unique company number; the registration record is published in the Commercial Registry database.
required_dossiers: Notarized incorporation contract
Name reservation certificate
Lease contract and landlord no-objection letter
Tax ID or national ID of the formation agent or founding shareholders
Commercial Registry application form duly signed
Notarized power of attorney for any non-resident foreign shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In the event of an administrative query or a request for special licenses, GAFI issues a 30-day curing notice; the applicant submits supplementary evidence through the one-stop shop; if the application is refused, the applicant may appeal to the GAFI Complaints and Appeals Committee within 30 days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Taxpayer Registration Offices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the unified tax registration application with the ETA to obtain the Tax Card, which records the income tax number and, where applicable, the VAT number for taxable services exceeding the statutory registration threshold (EGP 500,000 per annum); register as a withholding agent for salaries and foreign payments; apply for electronic invoice platform credentials and appoint the tax representative.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry certificate
ETA tax registration application form
Notarized lease contract
Managers' resolution appointing the tax representative
National ID or passport of the tax representative
Bank letter of account opening, if already opened
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Tax Card is delayed or queried, the taxpayer may submit a formal reminder accompanied by complete evidence to the local ETA directorate; rejection or penalty assessments may be appealed before the Internal Tax Committee within 30 days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI) – Local Insurance Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the LLC as an employer with NOSI within 30 days of the first hire using the Commercial Registry certificate; declare all managers and employees, obtain the employer social insurance number and individual insurance numbers; withhold employee contributions and transfer monthly insurance premiums; maintain payroll records consistent with Labor Law No. 12 of 2003.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry certificate
Tax Card
Notarized lease contract
List of managers and employees with national ID copies
NOSI Form 1 (employer registration form)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the employer misses the statutory 30-day registration deadline, NOSI may impose late penalties; the employer should file a penalty-reduction administrative request with an explanatory memorandum before the local Insurance Dispute Committee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sectoral Accreditations and Civil Defense Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Information Technology Industry Development Agency (ITIDA) – Electronic Signature and Data Protection Units; Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT) Data Protection Center; General Administration of Civil Defense, Ministry of Interior
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Determine whether the platform operates as an electronic signature verification or certification authority: if affirmative, apply for accreditation as an electronic signature service provider under Law No. 15 of 2004 and its Executive Regulations; concurrently register as a data controller/processor under Data Protection Law No. 151 of 2020; obtain the Civil Defense fire safety clearance for the registered office and submit the technical security audit documentation.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registry certificate and Tax Card
E-signature accreditation application with technical and security audit dossier
Data protection registration form covering data subject rights and breach response procedures
Civil Defense firm file, floor plans, fire extinguisher and alarm maintenance contracts
Official safety recommendation from a licensed fire safety engineer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For ITIDA or Data Protection Center rejections, the applicant may cure technical deficiencies within 30 days and resubmit; a refusal may be challenged before the Minister of Communications and Information Technology; Civil Defense clearance may be re-inspected after remediation by a licensed fire safety engineer.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Information Technology Industry Development Agency (ITIDA), Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT), in coordination with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI); no Industrial Development Authority manufacturing license is required for office-based software and cloud services.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Electronic Signature Service Provider Accreditation (Law No. 15 of 2004 and Executive Regulations) and Data Controller/Processor Registration Certificate (Data Protection Law No. 151 of 2020); supplemented by the Commercial Registry certificate and Tax Card for general software operations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C (Exemption / Registration) – office-based SaaS software development has no significant environmental impact; a full EIA report is not required; if the premises include independent backup power generators, an environmental screening form (Form B) must be filed with the EEAA for a registration-level assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process effluents for dry-office operations; sanitary wastewater must discharge to municipal sewers in compliance with Decree No. 44 of 2000 standards; waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE) must be transferred only to EEAA-licensed waste operators under Law No. 202 of 2020; any standby generator emissions must meet ambient air quality standards of Law No. 4 of 1994 as amended.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Required – Civil Defense fire safety certificate from the General Administration of Civil Defense (Ministry of Interior) confirming fire extinguishers, fire alarm systems, and evacuation plans; structural and electrical inspection clearance of the leased premises by a licensed engineer; and workplace compliance with Labor Law No. 12 of 2003 for safe working conditions, ventilation, lighting, and first-aid equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance; primary digital portal: www.eta.gov.eg; mandatory e-invoicing and e-receipt portal: invoicing.eta.gov.eg; unified corporate registration gateway administered by the General Authority for Investment (GAFI).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned LLC incorporates through the GAFI one-stop-shop, obtaining Commercial Registration, National ID, and Tax Card (TIN) in a single submission; ETA issues a 9-digit Tax Identification Number and an electronic tax file. In-person or e-registration via the unified registry triggers mandatory income tax registration within 30 days of commercial registration; VAT registration (Form 8) is mandatory once taxable supplies exceed EGP 500,000 per year and voluntary from EGP 100,000; e-invoicing onboarding with an ETA-issued digital signing certificate must follow. The LLC must also register for PAYE/social insurance (NASSCOM) and, if it has no Egyptian permanent establishment, appoint a local tax representative for withholding tax portability; all registrations require authenticated shareholder/manager ID, articles of association, and the lease/ownership proof of the Egyptian registered office.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - an Egyptian LLC is a resident taxpayer taxed on worldwide income under Law No. 91 of 2005 (as amended by Law No. 30 of 2023); the standard corporate income tax rate is 22.5%, with a temporary 25% rate applied to the slice of net taxable income exceeding EGP 20 million; dividends are not deductible at the entity level and distributions to non-residents are subject to 10% withholding tax (subject to treaty relief); no territorial or pass-through election is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election exists under Egyptian law. Permitted statutory elections include: (i) consolidated group filing for directly or indirectly owned 90%+ affiliates, subject to ETA pre-approval; (ii) declining-balance depreciation at 125% of the straight-line rate upon ETA consent; (iii) VAT cash-basis accounting for taxpayers with annual supplies below EGP 1,000,000; (iv) ordering of 5-year loss carry-forward utilization; and (v) foreign tax credit election for creditable foreign corporate income taxes against Egyptian CIT, capped at the Egyptian effective rate.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016, as amended, administered by the Egyptian Tax Authority
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual value of taxable supplies (mandatory registration, Article 15 of Law 67/2016); EGP 100,000 annual taxable supplies (voluntary registration); a non-resident supplier deriving Egyptian-source digital or SaaS revenue must register without a local threshold under the deemed-supplier rules for electronically supplied services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time fiscal clearance under ETA Decision No. 318 of 2020 and subsequent phased rollouts. All VAT-registered taxpayers, including non-resident e-service suppliers, must issue invoices in the ETA-approved XML or JSON schema, digitally sign each invoice with the ETA-issued certificate, transmit it via REST/SOAP API for instantaneous validation, and include the ETA-returned QR code in the customer-facing document; B2C transactions require the separate e-receipt stream. Cleared e-invoices are the exclusive basis for input VAT deduction; non-clearance or manual substitution invalidates the invoice and triggers penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and services are zero-rated at 0% under Article 29 of Law No. 67/2016. For the LegalTech SaaS/e-signature scope (ISIC 6201), zero-rating of cross-border services is available when: (i) the recipient is a non-resident without an Egyptian permanent establishment; (ii) the service is wholly performed and the economic benefit is realized outside Egypt, with no connection to Egyptian real estate, goods, or taxable activities; (iii) the consideration is received in freely convertible foreign currency and credited to an Egyptian bank account; and (iv) the pricing is at arm's length and documented for transfer pricing. Exporters of zero-rated supplies may reclaim attributable input VAT; refunds are processed through the ETA's electronic refund system, with a statutory 45-day review window for complete claims.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (Bayan) evidencing physical exit from Egypt, with ETA customs matching codes
Signed contract and itemized commercial invoice describing the exact digital/e-signature service and its non-Egyptian beneficiary
Foreign inward remittance certificate (Foreign Currency Remittance Advice) from an Egyptian bank showing settlement of the export consideration
Proof of offshore consumption, including IP address/geo-location of the beneficiary's usage for SaaS authentication events, service-level logs, and offshore server/delivery records
Zero-rated supply register (export ledger) reconciling e-invoices to banking and customs data
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA conducts data-driven audits reconciling e-invoice clearance files, customs declarations, banking remittance records, and server logs; zero-rating claims lacking full substantiation are rejected and the VAT becomes payable with monthly delay tax at 1.5% of the unpaid amount. Under Article 72 of Law 67/2016, fraudulent export claims carry administrative fines, retrospective clawback of all refunded input VAT for a 5-year look-back period, and criminal liability: imprisonment of up to 3 years and a fine of not less than EGP 20,000 and not more than EGP 200,000, or the full amount of evaded tax, whichever is greater; repeat offenders face doubled penalties and debarment from zero-rated export treatment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) — Arabic: البنك المركزي المصري; supreme regulator under Law No. 88 of 2003 (Central Banking, Banking, and Monetary System Law), as amended by Law No. 162 of 2020; sole authority for foreign-exchange licensing, banking licensing, balance-of-payments reporting, and administration of Egypt's unified flexible exchange-rate regime (floating since March 2024 under the IMF Extended Fund Facility).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Current-account transactions are effectively fully convertible: SaaS subscription receipts, software-licensing fees, e-signature service invoices, and other service-export proceeds can be credited directly to CBE-licensed Egyptian bank accounts in USD or other currencies without prior CBE approval, subject only to standard documentary verification (invoice, contract, proof of service delivery). Capital-account transactions are restricted in form rather than substance: (i) foreign direct investment (FDI) equity injections require registration via CBE Form 10, (ii) shareholder or intercompany loans require Form 12, (iii) profit and dividend remittance requires a valid CBE registration of the original injection, Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) tax-clearance certificates, audited financial statements, and board resolution, and (iv) non-resident settlement through offshore accounts is prohibited for export receipts — all export proceeds must be repatriated to Egypt. Since the March 2024 exchange-rate unification, there is no mandatory conversion of foreign currency to EGP and no surrender requirement; banks execute customer conversions at market-determined rates with no CBE price ceiling. Real remittance friction persists in documentary lead times of 3 to 10 business days rather than convertibility refusal.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Statutory repatriation window: 100% of each export invoice value must be received in Egypt through a licensed bank within 120 days (four months) from the export documentation date — bill of lading for goods, or tax invoice/service completion certificate for digital services (applicable to LegalTech SaaS and e-signature licensing). Mandatory conversion ratio: 0% — under CBE Board Decree No. 564 of 2022 (effective 1 January 2023), all export proceeds may be retained in the exporter's foreign-currency account and no surrender to the banking system is mandated; prior percentage-based surrender rules were abolished. Extensions beyond 120 days are grantable by the CBE through the relationship bank upon written justification (long-term SaaS contracts, milestone billing). Late or partial repatriation subjects the exporter to CBE penalties, loss of Export Support Fund privileges, and bank-level debarment of the account's foreign-currency clearing privileges.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency account (EGP/USD/EUR) + dedicated USD Capital Escrow Account for CBE Form 10 registration
Operational EGP/USD account; capital-proceeds escrow sub-account for FDI
Operational EGP/USD account and export-proceeds foreign-currency account
Operational EGP/USD account; trade-services desk for export documentation
Global multi-currency account with DDA/current-account sweep; USD capital-injection escrow desk
Operational account with ad-hoc FX forward lines

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW as a primary treasury rail; MODERATE as a supplementary collection/clearing sub-ledger. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise Platform, Payoneer, Stripe Treasury, Airwallex) are not CBE-licensed banks and cannot issue local Egyptian IBANs. CBE Law No. 88 of 2003 requires all export proceeds of Egyptian-resident entities to be repatriated to and settled through a licensed Egyptian bank; therefore, aggregate settlement received by an EMI must be swept (MT103 or SWIFT gpi) into the Egyptian bank account to satisfy the 120-day export-proceeds rule. Legal constraints: (i) EMIs cannot open EGP-denominated accounts for the Egyptian entity; (ii) no CBE Forms 10/12 registration can be executed through an EMI; (iii) Egyptian Data Protection Law No. 151/2020 and CBE payment-systems rules impose data localization and transaction-record requirements that offshore EMIs typically cannot meet for full statutory compliance; (iv) Stripe/Card receipts flowing through a foreign EMI must be mapped to underlying export invoices to avoid an 'unexplained foreign credit' AML flag. Recommended architecture: Stripe/Card settlement → offshore EMI/collection account → same-day SWIFT sweep → Egyptian Tier-1 bank (CIB or NBE) → EGP conversion via interbank market.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is MANDATORY. CBE AML regulations (Law No. 80 of 2002 and CBE AML Unit circulars) require all authorized signatories, the legal representative, and every UBO holding 25% or more to appear in person at the branch for biometric enrollment, original-document verification, and signature confirmation. No Egyptian Tier-1 bank offers fully remote corporate account opening. Non-resident directors who cannot travel may execute notarized powers of attorney (consular-legalized where required) conferring signing authority to a resident manager, provided the resident manager appears physically and hands over original corporate documents; the UBO disclosure declaration must still be signed by the ultimate natural persons, with notarization and apostille/consular legalization acceptable as substitute for physical attendance of the UBO only. At least one Egyptian-resident signatory with direct liability is expected, typically the general manager or CFO. Post-onboarding KYC reviews (annual and risk-triggered) are conducted remotely.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO chain opacity — foreign investors layered through multiple holding vehicles; failure to disclose ultimate natural persons interferes with Egyptian bank Customer Due Diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and consular-legalized (i) Certificate of Incorporation and Memorandum & Articles of Association of EG_LLC and each direct shareholder, (ii) Commercial Registry Extract issued ≤ 3 months, (iii) updated CBE-compliant UBO declaration identifying all natural persons holding ≥25% directly or indirectly, (iv) corporate-ownership diagram with percentage holdings, and (v) clean passport/National-ID copies plus six-month foreign bank reference statements for each UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border SaaS revenue concentration via aggregators (Stripe, Payoneer, PayPal) without per-transaction export invoices — triggers classification as unexplained foreign credits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Export-contract registry (signed SaaS agreements naming the Egyptian entity as licensor), platform payout statements (Stripe and Card settlement reports), service export invoices, a documented revenue-recognition policy, and a complete audit trail linking each aggregated payout to named overseas customers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds ambiguity for initial capital deposit, especially where capital arrives from a non-licensed offshore EMI or a third-country correspondent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Board resolution authorizing the capital injection, source-of-funds declaration letter (notarized), remitting bank's MT103/MT202 credit advice showing the ultimate remitter, signed shareholder loan agreement (if loan), and a completed CBE Form 10 / Form 12 application.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Virtual-office or minimal-physical-footprint red flag — LegalTech SaaS with no premises raises CTR/EAR concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered-head-office lease contract (notarized), utility bills matching the commercial-registry address, active ETA tax card (new format) proving tax-filing status, and social-insurance certificate evidencing actual employment of Egyptian staff.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injection (FDI equity or shareholder loan) is routed exclusively via SWIFT MT103 (customer transfer) from the foreign investor's bank to the CBE-licensed Egyptian bank, with instruction tags specifying: (a) beneficiary — EG_LLC's dedicated capital-escrow or foreign-currency account; (b) purpose code — E1 (equity with no option feature) or E2 (equity with option) for FDI, or D1-D8 for loan categories per CBE Balance-of-Payments reporting; (c) Remittance Information field 70: 'CAPITAL INJECTION — EG_LLC — CBE FORM 10' (or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN — FORM 12'). The receiving bank performs (i) legal-entity verification against commercial registry and CBE sanction lists, (ii) source-of-funds verification against the remitter name, (iii) negative-news screening, and (iv) issuance of the CBE Exchange Control registration certificate within 5 to 10 business days. Conversion to EGP is optional at market rate; full retention in USD is permissible. Verification package: notarized board resolution, updated Articles of Association showing issued capital, tax clearance certificate, and audited opening balance sheet.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For a LegalTech SaaS exporter, outbound trade payments are service-import disbursements (cloud infrastructure, e-signature certificate authorities, legal-content databases, sub-processing vendors). Recommended rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 (customer direct transfer) with CBE service-import purpose code and the underlying invoice/contract annexed to the bank's e-filing portal; (ii) for larger or letter-of-credit-mandated purchases — commercial documentary L/C (UCP600) with MT700 issuance; (iii) SEPA/SWIFT gpi for euro-denominated sub-vendor payments. Each outbound payment must be cross-referenced to a registered CBE debit note or related inbound capital inflow to evidence balance-of-payments matching; withholding tax (15% for technical-service fees to non-residents, 20% for royalties, subject to treaty reduction under Egypt's double-taxation network) must be certified by ETA Form 41 before bank release. EGP/USD conversion is executed automatically from the USD account using the bank's published market rate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable OTC FX forward contracts (USD/EGP, EUR/EGP) with CBE-licensed commercial banks, tenors up to 12 months, backed by documented underlying commercial or investment exposure (SaaS export invoices, capital-injection FX commitments).
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EGP or EUR/EGP) executed with licensed banks for medium-term hedging of subscription-contract receivables and intercompany loan revaluation risk.
OTC FX options (call/put on EGP) purchased solely from licensed Egyptian banks — option-premium payments are permissible, while writing or selling options is restricted.
Natural hedging via staggered multi-currency liquidity pools (EGP/USD/EUR) and matched invoicing — maintaining USD-denominated SaaS contracts to offset EGP depreciation without derivative cost.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Tax Law No. 91/2005, as amended)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after the end of the fiscal year; for calendar-year taxpayers, no later than 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge of up to 2% per month on the settled tax; late payment interest at the Central Bank discount rate plus a statutory increment; enforced collection, attachment of bank accounts, and criminal liability for willful failure to file.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local Tax Office under the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 January; the tax card must be valid for the current calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An expired tax card may block issuance of clearance certificates, public-sector contracts, import/export privileges, and permit renewals; administrative fines may be imposed by the tax office.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approved Audited Financial Statements Filed with the Investment Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the company's fiscal year end; for calendar-year entities, by 30 June, including shareholders' annual meeting approval.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to deposit audited financial statements may prevent issuance of good-standing certificates, delay share transfers, trigger administrative penalties, and expose the LLC to judicial strike-off proceedings before the Economic Court.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Beneficial Ownership Register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 January following the reporting year, and within 30 days of any change in ultimate beneficial ownership or shareholding transfers.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under AML Law No. 80/2002 and its implementing regulations; suspension of corporate registry services until compliance; in severe cases, criminal liability for money-laundering-related reporting violations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No turnover or capital threshold exemption applies to Egyptian LLCs; every LLC must appoint at least one certified auditor to examine and report on the annual financial statements before submission to the shareholders' meeting and GAFI.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Financial Reporting Standards (EFRS), substantially aligned with IFRS; statutory accounting records must be maintained in Arabic with amounts in Egyptian pounds or an approved functional currency.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The LLC must maintain a current beneficial ownership register at its registered office. Every share transfer or change in control must be recorded in the members' ledger, supported by notarized transfer documentation, and reported to GAFI within 30 days. An annual UBO confirmation filing with GAFI is mandatory regardless of whether a transfer occurred during the year; the confirmation must list all ultimate natural-person owners and material controllers.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 – USD 800 per year for a licensed registered office and corporate agent in Cairo or Alexandria
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 800 – USD 2,500 per year for a single-purpose LegalTech SaaS entity with low transaction volume

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: CIT holiday of up to 5 years for eligible new information-technology and investment projects under Investment Incentives Law No. 72/2017; an additional deduction of up to 50% of investment cost for projects in promoted governorates or strategic sectors; free-zone and Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZone) projects may be subject to an annual 1%-3% gross-revenue fee in lieu of CIT; no preferential reduced rate applies to LegalTech SaaS revenue outside these incentive regimes.
